title: fix(lint,objectql)!: a validation rule reading a field its lookup target does not declare is refused at save, and no longer leaves its sibling rules without a verdict
body:
Fixes #24468

Clause-②: no (narrowing) (the save door newly refuses a validation rule it accepted; owes one `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review, on the narrowing face, before the queue)

Dispatched by the `domain:engine` seat 1 PM (claim 6262728643, `session_01JtSQQ3EWsbNPzyYMug1tXy`). Developer session: `session_01XPyxHgkHDoFuEza6RvCJtd`. This is the predicate-seam twin of #24410 (PR #24466, `45bec43cd9`), and it follows that PR's pattern.

## What changes

**Engine: per-rule isolation (`packages/objectql`).** `resolvePredicateRelated` reads, per reference, the union of the related columns every validation rule reads. When one column was undeclared on the target, `resolveOneHopRelated` answered the whole reference `undeclared-field`. Every rule through that lookup then had no verdict and refused the write, naming the other rule's field.

- `resolvePredicateRelated` now takes the undeclared columns out of the shared read, using the shared `undeclaredRelatedFields` helper (no second definition of "declared"). It lists them on the binding as `undeclaredFields`. The loader reads the declared rest under `authority: 'predicate'`, with the same bound as before.
- `resolveTraversalScope` (`validation/rule-validator.ts`, the binding's consumer) first refuses a rule only for its OWN undeclared columns, naming only those. A rule naming none of them is judged on the row exactly as it is alone.
- A reference whose every read column is undeclared still gets a binding (`unavailable: 'undeclared-field'`), so no rule meets a bare id.
- ⛔ Not moved: the formula seam (`resolveFormulaRelated`, `formulaHopScope`), `resolveOneHopRelated`, and the predicate read's authority and bound. No undeclared column enters the system-authority read.

**Lint: save-door refusal (`packages/lint`, the `domain:spec` rider declared in 6262742638).** `refuseUndeclaredHopField` (#24410) now also runs in `check()` wherever `traversalHydration` is set. Those are a `script` / `cross_field` rule's `condition`, at the top level and inside a `conditional`'s `then` / `otherwise`. It judges the hop column against the target's field index (declared fields, injected columns and `id`) under the existing `expression-invalid` rule, with no new code.

- The message opens with the shared validator's "unknown field" words, naming the column and the target, then names the reference read. Its consequence clause is per site: a rule "has no verdict and every write it judges is refused". The formula message is byte-identical to before.
- One body serves `os validate`, `os build` and the object save door.
- A target the stack does not carry is not judged: a missed catch, never a false refusal.
- A reference read more than one hop deep is left to the traversal checks' own refusal (one finding, not two). This applies to the formula site too, where it only removes a duplicate finding on an expression already refused.

**Census rows.** objectql `federated-injected-column-readers.test.ts` gets one row for the new engine use, `engine.ts#resolvePredicateRelated :: referenceTargetOf()` → `caller-predicate`. `packages/core`'s `[#22661]` census is per file, and both caller files (`engine.ts`, `validate-expressions.ts`) already have rows. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/core test:repo` passed 82/82.

## Measurement (M, booted composition: `packages/qa/dogfood/test/rule-hop-undeclared-related-field.dogfood.test.ts`)

Fixture: `rrh_order` with a lookup `account` to `rrh_account` (declares `status`). It carries two `script` rules: `open_account` reads `record.account.status`, which is declared, and `north_only` reads `record.account.region`, which is not.

| Reading | Before (`45bec43cd9`) | After (`69f76c6ef`) |
|---|---|---|
| `PUT /meta/object/rrh_order_saved` with both rules | `200` (saved) | `422 INVALID_METADATA`, one `expression-invalid` issue at `validation 'north_only'`, message opens "unknown field `region` on `rrh_account`" |
| Control: same PUT with only `open_account` | `200` | `200` |
| Control: `open_account` alone, open / closed account | `201` / `400` with its own message | `201` / `400` with its own message |
| Stored copy, open account | `400`: BOTH rules "could not be evaluated ('rrh_account' declares no 'region')" | `400`: only `north_only`, naming `region`; `open_account` absent |
| Stored copy, closed account | not reached (the pin stopped at the open-account row) | `400`: `open_account`'s own message, plus `north_only`'s refusal |

The before run on `45bec43cd9` had 3 of 4 pins red. The save door answered 200, and the stored copy's open-account write was refused with `open_account` "could not be evaluated ... declares no 'region'". The control's red was the pin's own `200` vs `201` create status, corrected before the after run. The after run is 4/4, with the #24410 formula pin also green (7/7).

**Ablations** (each through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, `ablation-dist-preflight.mjs` marker present in dist, restored to the HEAD blob with `git diff HEAD` empty, then rebuilt with the marker absent from dist):

- **A, per-rule isolation** (the `named.delete` of the undeclared columns removed in `resolvePredicateRelated`). 3 engine pins red (`engine-predicate-relationship.test.ts`, the `[#24468]` block), and the booted sibling pin red.
- **B, lint refusal** (the `refuseUndeclaredHopField(..., 'rule')` call removed). 3 lint pins red (`validate-expressions.rule-one-hop.test.ts`, and both LIT pins in `runtime-gate.object-validation-writes.test.ts`), and the booted save-door pin red.
- Restore: `git status --porcelain` clean, both markers absent from dist, booted pin 4/4.

## Pins

- `packages/objectql/src/engine-predicate-relationship.test.ts`, `[#24468]` block, on the real engine:
  - the valid sibling admits when it admits alone, and refuses with its own message;
  - the bad rule names only `not_a_column`;
  - one system read, projecting `['id', 'type']`.
- `packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-relationship-traversal.test.ts`, `[#24468]` block, on the binding contract: verdicts per rule; the bad rule names only its own field when the binding lists two; a fully undeclared reference still refuses.
- `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.rule-one-hop.test.ts`, on the build:
  - refusal naming field and target;
  - `id` and `created_at` admitted;
  - a target outside the stack not judged.
- `packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.object-validation-writes.test.ts`, `#24468` block, at the save door:
  - a target from another package in the closure, beside its valid sibling;
  - a nested `conditional` → `then`;
  - the control.
- `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.test.ts`: the `#5017` receiver census registers the refusal's `analysis` local as plumbing.
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/rule-hop-undeclared-related-field.dogfood.test.ts`: the booted pin above. Test-only; declared to `domain:cli` by the seat at review.

**Pin sweep.** The whole-reference `undeclared-field` verdict for a rule is pinned in two places, and both still hold:

- `rule-relationship-traversal.test.ts` hands a single-rule binding by hand.
- `engine-predicate-relationship.test.ts` "never smuggles an UNDECLARED field" has one rule, whose own field is undeclared.

No other test asserts the sibling refusal.

## Other predicate surfaces that read through a lookup

Probed with `validateStackExpressions`:

- **Not reached, and not needed:** a field-rule slot (`requiredWhen`) or an option `visibleWhen` through a lookup is already refused whole at save. Nothing hydrates there; the message says "a field-level predicate never reads the related record". This pass does not run there.
- **Not reached:** a `conditional` rule's `when` is opted out of hydration by the existing walk (`checkConditional` evaluates it unhydrated), so this pass does not judge it. See the acceptance notes.

All exited 0.

## Changesets

- `@objectstack/lint` `minor`, `fix(lint)!:`, BREAKING (an accept-set narrowing), with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. Its ADR-0087 marker is `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. It carries a FROM → TO and a "What to do".
- `@objectstack/objectql` `patch`, `Clause-②: no` with no arm.

## Acceptance notes

- A `conditional` rule's `when` that reads through a lookup is not hydrated (`checkConditional`), and the lint opts it out of the traversal checks. So `when: record.account.status == 'x'` saves clean, and it meets the bare id at evaluation. This is read from the code (the walk's own comment says it), not run as a failing probe. It is outside this card's two seams.
- The lint pass does not see a target field that an `objectExtensions` entry contributes at `os build` / `os validate`, as for the formula site (#24410's changeset says the same). The save door judges the merged object.
